chapter: Erroll Garner and the Los Angeles scene
title: Playing and recording with Garner
summary: They played Gene Norman concerts and McGhee praises his accompaniment.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: How about you and Erroll playing together? Did you get to play together?
Yeah, we played together a lot. I think we made some records together, too.
Well, there were some of the jam sessions...the concerts.
The concerts, yeah. We played on them...
"Blue Lou" and those things in that period...
Yeah. Well, those things were recorded at...
...Gene Norman's thing, yeah. Which was delightful, because Erroll played his can off on the date.
Mostly he was known as a soloist and a leader of a trio. But he was great in a band, too.
Oh yeah, he was good. Very good.
How would you say he differed from the pianists of that time, like Bud Powell, Al Haig, Hank Jones, as far as comping for the soloist?

Well, I don't know. Erroll was a very beautiful comp, man. But I don't know whether I could say he was as good as Bud Powell or them guys, because they were strictly instrumental pianists, and they weren't out just to sound good... Like, Erroll had his show going, and he was making money with it.
Well, I wasn't even trying to say good or better, but just like a different kind of approach to backing up the soloist because of his style.

Oh yeah. But he was magnificent. He was beautiful. I loved to play with Erroll, because he knew where to put the right things. Whatever you played, if you was playing and he wanted to complement you, he could do it, you know...
Now, after California, did you see him in New York over the years?

Yeah. I saw him, oh, several times here in New York. In fact, when I moved back to New York, we saw each other quite often. Like, we went to Paris together and everything. We had a ball, man. He was a nice cat.
